newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIAN LEU FIRMS SLIGHTLY AT CLOSE.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIAN LEU FIRMS SLIGHTLY AT CLOSE.

text.p: The Romanian leu currency closed on Thursday at 7,040/7,070 lei to the dollar, slightly firmer on its 7,050/80 opening quote, in a market where the dollar supply was outrunning demand, operators said.
"Dollar buyers might emerge if the central bank started draining excess leu funds," one trader said. "Then, trading would be more active."
Latest central bank data showed the foreign exchange interbank volume was $5.3 million on Wednesday, when overall turnover amounted $24.6 million.
Traders expected the market would remain almost unchanged on Friday, with no market moving factors ahead.
On the money market, one-week rates hovered around 82 percent with traders seeing the rates slipping slightly over the next few days due to overliquidity on the market.
Leu rates at currency retail shops averaged 6,950/7,100 to the dollar.
Local operators said the market remained unmoved by the recent falls in the Czech crown due to speculative sellings.

"The depreciated Czech crown failed to impress our market mainly," one trader said. "It is normal, as we do not have extensive trade links with the Czech Republic. Also, the economic situation of the two countries is different," one trader said.

The local market barely reacts to internal news, the trader said. "The market might react to swings in the Czech crown only after Romania becomes effectively active within the Central European Free Trade Accord.
Earlier in the day, the Czech National Bank (CNB) limited the access of non-resident investors to the local money market as part of its efforts to back up the Czech crown.
The CNB fixed the crown at 30.629 to the dollar and 18.081 to the mark on Thursday, implying a deviation against basket parity of -3.00 percent after a fixing 0f -2.27 percent on Wednesday.
